title: Daily automatic backup, with last-backup time and a one-tap backup on the dashboard
description: Product Owner request: should backup run automatically, daily; show the last backup time on the home screen with a small icon to back up from there. RECOMMENDED: yes, and it is the single highest-value safety feature left. Today backup is entirely manual - BackupScreen fires ActivityResultContracts.CreateDocument, the warden picks a location, and nothing records that it happened. A warden who forgets for two months has two months of unrecoverable data on one phone, and nothing in the app tells them so. WHY IT NEEDS A DESIGN, not just a WorkManager job: the current export takes a one-shot Uri from CreateDocument and no persistable permission is taken, so there is no folder to write to unattended. The job needs a location chosen ONCE via OpenDocumentTree with takePersistableUriPermission, stored in a new BackupPreferences, and reused daily. Everything else reuses BackupManager.export() as-is. THE REAL RISK is not the job failing, it is the job failing SILENTLY - a warden who believes they are covered and is not, is worse off than one who knows they are not. So the dashboard tile is not decoration, it is the feature: it must show staleness and failure as prominently as success, using the existing RAG tokens (recent = green, getting old = amber, never/failed/very stale = red). SUGGESTED SHAPE: (1) pick a folder once, persisted; (2) daily WorkManager job, same pattern as LODGY-15/59/60; (3) skip the run when nothing has changed since the last backup, so identical zips are not churned daily - the zip carries photos and is not small; (4) keep a rolling window of the last N backups and delete older ones, or storage grows without bound; (5) if the folder becomes unwritable - card removed, folder deleted, permission revoked - surface that on the dashboard rather than retrying quietly. RELATION TO LODGY-66: this is the auto-export measure recommended there. It also strengthens the case against soft delete, because a recent automatic backup covers the accidental-deletion fear that a recycle bin was meant to address, without taxing every query in the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Warden picks a backup folder once; the permission persists across reboots and app updates, and the choice is changeable later from More
A daily WorkManager job writes a timestamped backup zip into that folder without any interaction, following the existing periodic-worker pattern
The dashboard shows when the last backup succeeded, in plain relative language, with a backup icon that runs one immediately
The dashboard indicator distinguishes recent, getting stale, and never-or-failed using the LODGY-36 status tokens, so a silently broken backup is visible rather than assumed fine
A run is skipped when no data has changed since the last successful backup, so unchanged days do not accumulate identical zips
Only the most recent N backups are kept; older ones are removed so the folder does not grow without bound
If the folder becomes unwritable the failure is surfaced on the dashboard and the warden is told how to re-pick it - it never fails silently
Backward compatible: an existing install that has never chosen a folder keeps working exactly as today, prompted but never blocked, and no migration is required beyond the new preference

history.note: Requested by the PO: daily auto-backup, last-backup time on the home screen with a one-tap backup icon. Filed with a recommended design and the silent-failure risk called out, because an auto-backup a warden wrongly believes is running is worse than no auto-backup.

Cross-reference: LODGY-76 (forgotten PIN) is another argument for this ticket. A warden locked out of their own app loses everything only if there is no recent backup - with a daily automatic one, a forgotten PIN costs them the app state and nothing else.
